Title: Create a recoverable Unreal project shell
Body:
## Objective
Create the complete current-Unreal project context that is missing from this checkout.

## Epic
Stream MVP - Project and Analysis Foundation

## Scope
- Choose and record the exact Unreal Engine version.
- Create a C++ project with the `SynRTCQT` name or document the new module boundary.
- Enable Audio Synesthesia and Movie Render Queue.
- Preserve `.uproject`, target files, `Config/`, and source in a recoverable location.
- Decide which binary assets require Git LFS or external storage.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The editor opens after closing and reopening the project.
- A Development Editor build succeeds for the clean shell.
- The engine version and enabled plugins are documented.
- Another clone or backup contains everything needed to recreate the shell.

## Dependencies
- Unreal Engine installation and C++ toolchain.

## Out Of Scope
- Making the old custom RTCQT module compile.
- Final visual design.

## Evidence
- Attach the successful build log and editor screenshot.

Title: Prepare a licensed test track and ConstantQNRT asset
Body:
## Objective
Create the approved, pre-analyzed audio input for the first visualizer.

## Epic
Stream MVP - Project and Analysis Foundation

## Scope
- Select a 30-60 second WAV that is owned or cleared for broadcast.
- Import it into `Content/Audio/`.
- Create and configure a ConstantQNRT asset with 32 or 48 bands.
- Record the track duration, sample rate, and permission source.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The SoundWave plays in the editor.
- ConstantQNRT analysis completes without an editor error.
- Band values can be queried at three or more timestamps.
- Broadcast permission is recorded next to the asset.

## Dependencies
- Recoverable Unreal project shell.

## Out Of Scope
- Final music selection.
- Custom RTCQT analysis.

## Evidence
- Attach the asset settings screenshot and three sampled value results.

Title: Build the first ConstantQNRT line visualizer
Body:
## Objective
Show one stable mesh response per ConstantQNRT frequency band.

## Epic
Stream MVP - Deterministic Visualizer

## Scope
- Create a visualizer actor using Blueprint or focused C++.
- Create one cube instance per band in a line layout.
- Query band values at the current song time.
- Map values to Z scale with bounded minimum and maximum values.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every configured band has exactly one visible mesh.
- A test tone or music segment produces obvious band-specific motion.
- No mesh is created or destroyed during normal playback.
- The actor handles a missing analyzer asset without crashing.

## Dependencies
- Licensed test track and ConstantQNRT asset.

## Out Of Scope
- Circle, spiral, and sphere layouts.
- Old RTCQT C++ integration.

## Evidence
- Attach a short editor capture and actor/component screenshot.

Title: Lock playback and analysis to one clock
Body:
## Objective
Make repeated playback produce the same visual timing.

## Epic
Stream MVP - Deterministic Visualizer

## Scope
- Define one authoritative song-time source.
- Query ConstantQNRT using that time.
- Handle start, stop, seek, and restart without a free-running animation timer.
- Add a lightweight timestamp or band-value debug capture.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Three runs of the same 30-second segment align at selected checkpoints.
- Restart returns the visualizer to the expected first-frame state.
- Seeking does not leave stale smoothed values behind.
- The clock choice is documented in the visualizer notes.

## Dependencies
- First ConstantQNRT line visualizer.

## Evidence
- Attach checkpoint timestamps or debug captures from three runs.

Title: Add spectrum smoothing and response controls
Body:
## Objective
Make the visualization readable without losing timing or band identity.

## Epic
Stream MVP - Deterministic Visualizer

## Scope
- Add attack and release smoothing.
- Add noise floor, response exponent, and min/max scale controls.
- Reset temporal state on stop and seek.
- Expose settings in the actor or a small settings asset.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Controls update without rebuilding the actor.
- Silence settles to the configured baseline.
- Peaks remain bounded at the configured maximum.
- Repeated runs with unchanged settings remain deterministic.

## Dependencies
- Single-clock visualizer.

## Notes
Use the old `SpectrumProcessor` behavior as a reference, not a required port.

Title: Build the emissive material and exposure baseline
Body:
## Objective
Create a bright, stream-readable material response without unstable exposure.

## Epic
Stream MVP - Deterministic Visualizer

## Scope
- Create a material with emissive intensity and color controls.
- Feed per-band response through dynamic material parameters or per-instance custom data.
- Lock or deliberately configure scene exposure.
- Test against the intended stream background.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Emissive response follows the same band values as mesh scale.
- No clipping or unreadable black frames appear in a short render.
- Exposure does not visibly pump during the test segment.
- Material parameter names and ranges are documented.

## Dependencies
- Line visualizer and response controls.

## Evidence
- Attach stills from quiet, average, and peak moments.

Title: Build a track-length Level Sequence
Body:
## Objective
Put the visualizer, camera, and audio into a sequence with an exact shared duration.

## Epic
Stream MVP - Render and OBS Launch

## Scope
- Create a Level Sequence matching the test track duration.
- Add the camera and lock the intended framing.
- Define how audio playback and visualizer song time are driven by the sequence.
- Add start and end handles only if the final media specification includes them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Sequence duration matches the intended output duration.
- Frame rate and resolution are explicitly set.
- Scrubbing to known timestamps shows the expected visual state.
- Camera framing has no clipped or missing band meshes.

## Dependencies
- Deterministic visualizer and material baseline.

## Evidence
- Attach sequence settings and camera-frame screenshots.

Title: Render a short synchronization proof
Body:
## Objective
Prove Movie Render Queue can produce a clean, repeatable 30-second visual render.

## Epic
Stream MVP - Render and OBS Launch

## Scope
- Configure Movie Render Queue for the target frame rate and resolution.
- Render a frame sequence or high-quality intermediate.
- Record render settings and elapsed time.
- Inspect first, middle, and last frames for missing content or temporal jumps.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The render completes without missing frames.
- Output duration matches the selected sequence range.
- The same range can be rendered again from saved settings.
- No editor overlays, debug text, or unintended UI appear.

## Dependencies
- Track-length Level Sequence.

## Evidence
- Attach the MRQ preset, render log, and proof clip.

Title: Produce and verify the synchronized media file
Body:
## Objective
Combine the clean visual render with the original approved audio for OBS playback.

## Epic
Stream MVP - Render and OBS Launch

## Scope
- Encode the rendered frames or intermediate into the chosen delivery codec.
- Mux the original WAV or approved master audio exactly once.
- Check synchronization near the start, middle, and end.
- Record codec, resolution, frame rate, audio format, and duration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The file plays from start to finish without corruption.
- Video and audio duration agree within one frame or a documented tolerance.
- Three synchronization checkpoints pass.
- Loudness and peak levels are safe for the intended stream mix.

## Dependencies
- Completed synchronization proof render.

## Out Of Scope
- OBS scene configuration.

## Evidence
- Attach media metadata and checkpoint notes.

Title: Build the OBS scene and audio routing
Body:
## Objective
Play the synchronized visual in OBS with predictable video and exactly one audio path.

## Epic
Stream MVP - Render and OBS Launch

## Scope
- Add the final file as a Media Source.
- Configure loop, restart-on-activation, and visibility behavior.
- Choose either embedded media audio or a separate routed track, not both.
- Set canvas, output resolution, frame rate, and color settings.
- Create a basic fallback scene.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The source starts at the expected frame when the scene is activated.
- Audio meters show one intended signal path with no doubling or echo.
- A local recording has the expected resolution, frame rate, and sync.
- Switching to the fallback scene takes only one operator action.

## Dependencies
- Verified synchronized media file.

## Evidence
- Attach OBS source settings, audio mixer screenshot, and local test recording.

Title: Pass a private stream rehearsal
Body:
## Objective
Validate the complete viewer path before a public broadcast.

## Epic
Stream MVP - Render and OBS Launch

## Scope
- Run an unlisted or private stream for at least one full media loop.
- Watch from a second device or account.
- Monitor dropped frames, encoder load, audio levels, and sync.
- Test the fallback scene and recovery back to the main visual.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The full loop reaches the viewer without interruption.
- No doubled audio, clipping, or visible drift is observed.
- OBS reports no unexplained render or encoding lag.
- Fallback and recovery both work during the rehearsal.
- Any issue found becomes a separate card before public launch.

## Dependencies
- OBS scene and audio routing.

## Evidence
- Attach rehearsal date, platform, OBS stats, and viewer-side notes.

Title: Write the live-show runbook and fallback scene
Body:
## Objective
Make the first public use repeatable under time pressure.

## Epic
Stream MVP - Render and OBS Launch

## Scope
- Write preflight, go-live, scene-switch, recovery, and shutdown steps.
- Keep a known-good fallback visual and audio state.
- Record where the final media and OBS scene backup are stored.
- Add a short post-show checklist for logs and notes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A dry run can be completed using only the runbook.
- The fallback has no missing media or silent unexpected state.
- Paths and backup locations are valid on the streaming machine.
- The runbook records the last rehearsal result.

## Dependencies
- Passed private stream rehearsal.

Title: Add circle and spiral layouts
Body:
## Objective
Recover recognizable RTCQT visual layouts on the proven visualizer architecture.

## Epic
Polish - RTCQT Visual Language

## Scope
- Add circle and spiral layout modes.
- Keep band ordering and focus behavior explicit.
- Preserve the same analysis, smoothing, and material pipeline.
- Verify camera framing for each layout.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Layout switching does not recreate analysis state.
- Every band maps to one valid transform in each layout.
- Index zero and empty focus ranges are handled safely.
- A short MRQ test succeeds for both layouts.

## Dependencies
- Stream MVP visualizer is stable.

## Notes
Use `AMeshController` as design reference; do not copy known unsafe indexing.

Title: Evaluate custom RTCQT processing against the NRT baseline
Body:
## Objective
Decide with evidence whether any old custom processing is worth porting.

## Epic
Polish - RTCQT Visual Language

## Scope
- Identify two or three old processing features with likely visual value.
- Reproduce comparable settings using the current NRT pipeline where possible.
- Capture side-by-side clips on the same audio segment.
- Record visual benefit, complexity, packaging risk, and performance cost.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each candidate has a side-by-side result or a documented reason it cannot be tested.
- The decision names specific features to port or explicitly closes the port path.
- No old DSP work is required for the existing stream scene to continue working.

## Dependencies
- Passed Stream MVP and stable spectrum controls.

## Evidence
- Attach comparison clips and the decision note.

Title: Port only approved RTCQT spectrum features
Body:
## Objective
Add only the custom processing features that showed a material benefit in comparison tests.

## Epic
Polish - RTCQT Visual Language

## Scope
- Put analysis or shaping code behind a clean runtime module boundary.
- Keep editor-only dependencies out of runtime builds.
- Add known-signal tests for each approved feature.
- Preserve the ConstantQNRT path as a working fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Known test tones activate expected bands or shaping behavior.
- Development Editor and packaged runtime dependency boundaries are clean.
- The fallback NRT mode still renders the proven stream scene.
- A comparison render confirms the intended visual improvement.

## Dependencies
- Approved RTCQT processing decision.

## Out Of Scope
- Porting every surviving old class.

Title: Benchmark live Unreal capture in OBS
Body:
## Objective
Measure whether the visualizer can run live on the streaming machine without harming broadcast quality.

## Epic
Live - Real-Time and Interactive Delivery

## Scope
- Package or run the visualizer in a controlled full-screen or windowed mode.
- Capture it in OBS using the appropriate source type.
- Measure Unreal frame time, GPU load, OBS render lag, encoder lag, and audio sync.
- Compare results with the proven pre-rendered Media Source scene.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A 30-minute test records all target metrics.
- Quality thresholds and machine specifications are documented.
- The decision is explicit: use live capture, optimize and retest, or retain pre-rendered playback.
- The pre-rendered fallback remains immediately available.

## Dependencies
- Passed Stream MVP rehearsal.

## Evidence
- Attach OBS stats, Unreal performance captures, and decision notes.

Title: Prototype Pixel Streaming on the local network
Body:
## Objective
Prove one shared Unreal visualizer session can reach a browser before planning public hosting.

## Epic
Live - Real-Time and Interactive Delivery

## Scope
- Enable and configure Pixel Streaming for the chosen Unreal version.
- Connect one browser client over the local network.
- Confirm synchronized video and audio delivery.
- Disable general viewer control or limit it to one curated interaction.
- Record signaling, firewall, and GPU requirements discovered.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A second device receives the same visual and audio session.
- End-to-end latency and stability are measured for at least 15 minutes.
- Unwanted keyboard and mouse control is blocked.
- Public hosting, HTTPS, STUN/TURN, moderation, and access control remain separate follow-up work.

## Dependencies
- Stable live visualizer path and completed live-capture benchmark.

## Out Of Scope
- Public deployment and true multiplayer.
